newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Monti to step up single market pressure.
newsitem.headline: Monti to step up single market pressure.

text.p: European Union Internal Market Commissioner Mario Monti plans to step up public pressure on member states to implement and comply with single market rules by publishing regularly how each of them is performing.

The proposal will be part of the Commission's action plan for the completion of the single market which will be presented to EU leaders at the European Council in Amsterdam on June 16-17, a Commission official said on Monday.

The aim of publishing a weighted indicator on how member states fulfil single market rules would be to have a clearer picture of the failures and successes of individual countries to live up to the rules of the single market.

Such an indicator, which could be published for example every three months, would include not only the transposition of single market legislation but also for example the number of infringement cases and complaints against member states.

"If member governments do not like the adverse publicity that could arise from such transparency measures, the answer is very simple - they just have to make sure that they respect the rules and correct violations if they arise," Monti told the Financial Times newspaper.

In its Communication on the impact and effectiveness of the single market published last October, the Commission expressed concern about "inadequate transposition" of single market rules in member states.
"Substantial delays have occurred and poor quality transposition is also preventing business from fully exploiting the potential of the single market," it said.
